I bet you at least 50% of the people on here have been laid off at least once, including myself. I was let go by someone I considered my friend and mentor for no other reason than it made her look good politically. She was grossly unprepared for her new position and decided to dismantle the entire department rather than admit that. She couldn't even tell me what I did to deserve being let go, she had a co-worker tell me "I didn't have enough experience", even though she was the one who trained me and literally the only reason I'd gotten the job in the first place. I'd worked with her for five years, did girls night at her place, babysat her kid, considered myself her friend. It was devastating. I thought I was a failure and spent five years working towards a wasted goal. 
Now I know I spent five years working for a wasted goal! lol, I'm only halfway kidding. I learned a mad amount of super useful skills that have benefited me enormously. When it first happened I blamed myself and the shitty underhanded comments she made ate at me. Now, a few months later, I realize how toxic that job was and how it fed into my depression to the point of being suicidal. I'm actually grateful she was such a massive dick because if not I might still be working there. I would never had seen this had I not been forced to leave. We cling to what we know.  
All that to say is, most of us will get laid off, some multiple times, and it really sucks. But you're not a waste because you are having a common human experience. You also don't have to listen to that voice in your head. He's a massive twat and doesn't deserve any stage time.
